questions.q: Protecting the environment is a Fundamental Duty under:
questions.explanation: **51A(g)**; Article 48A is the Directive Principle on the environment.
questions.fact_text: **Art. 48A** (Directive Principle) asks the State to protect the environment, forests and wildlife; **Art. 51A(g)** makes protecting the environment a Fundamental Duty.

also.text: The SC called cracker-bursting a religious practice for Deepavali but held that **Art. 25(1)** is a 'qualified' right, subject to public order, morality and health, and must be read with **Art. 21** (right to a healthy environment).

questions.q: How many States have a Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: **Six**: Maharashtra, U.P., Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.
questions.fact_text: Six States have a Legislative Council: **Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka** (Art. 168). 28 Council seats were contested last week in UP, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka.

also.text: **Art. 169**: Parliament creates or abolishes a Council by ordinary law, after the State Assembly passes a resolution by a **two-thirds majority**.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Legislative Councils:
1. Parliament creates or abolishes a Council by ordinary law under Article 169.
2. The State Assembly must first pass a resolution by a two-thirds majority.
Which is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both are correct; such a law is **not** treated as a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
questions.fact_text: **Art. 169**: Parliament creates or abolishes a Council by ordinary law, after the State Assembly passes a resolution by a **two-thirds majority**.

also.text: **Art. 171**: Council strength at most **one-third** of the Assembly and at least **40**. Members: 1/3 elected by local bodies, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, 1/3 by MLAs, 1/6 nominated by the Governor.

questions.q: What share of a Legislative Council's members are elected by graduates?
questions.explanation: **1/12** by graduates and 1/12 by teachers; 1/3 by local bodies, 1/3 by MLAs, 1/6 nominated.
questions.fact_text: **Art. 171**: Council strength at most **one-third** of the Assembly and at least **40**. Members: 1/3 elected by local bodies, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, 1/3 by MLAs, 1/6 nominated by the Governor.

also.text: **Art. 172**: a permanent House, never dissolved. Members serve **6 years**; one-third retire every **2 years**. Ministers, including the CM, can be Council members.

questions.q: A member of a Legislative Council serves a term of:
questions.explanation: **6 years**; one-third retire every 2 years. The Council is never dissolved.
questions.fact_text: **Art. 172**: a permanent House, never dissolved. Members serve **6 years**; one-third retire every **2 years**. Ministers, including the CM, can be Council members.

also.text: Weak powers: no joint sitting, the Assembly's version prevails, and the Council can delay a bill by at most **four months**.

questions.q: On a Money Bill, a Legislative Council can:
options: Send it to a joint sitting
questions.explanation: It can only **recommend** within **14 days** (Article 198).
questions.fact_text: Delay power comes from **Art. 197** (3 months, then 1 month on re-passage). On Money Bills the Council can only recommend (**Art. 198**, 14 days).

also.text: Weak powers: no joint sitting, the Assembly's version prevails, and the Council can delay a bill by at most **four months**.

questions.q: Bicameral legislatures in six provinces were created by the:

also.text: Tamil Nadu's Council was abolished in **1986** (MGR as CM); a 2010 revival resolution was reversed in 2011. Andhra Pradesh's was abolished in **1985** (NTR) and re-created in **2007**.

questions.q: The Siang Upper Multipurpose Project is in:

also.text: A 36-hour bandh shut Upper Siang district against the project; the local **Adi** community fears losing land. Protests also target the **Subansiri Upper** project.
